desc_zh: 为钢琴入门练琴预设 80 BPM 4/4 拍，传统鼓点模式帮你听清每个强拍，配套哈农、车尔尼、拜厄等教材的慢练章节起步速度。
desc_en: Pre-set metronome page for piano practice — 80 BPM, 4/4, traditional drum. The starting tempo for Hanon, Czerny, and Beyer technique books.
narrative_zh:
刚开始跟节拍练琴，节奏不稳是最大的拦路虎。

80 BPM 是公认的入门起步速度——哈农、车尔尼、拜厄这些基本功教材的慢练章节大多落在这个区间。低于这个速度练起来太拖沓，再快又容易赶拍子。新手如果直接跳到 100 BPM，两周后多半会发现自己音阶弹出节拍不稳、节拍器被嫌弃成摆设。

这个页面已经帮你预设好了：80 BPM、4/4 拍、传统鼓点。每个小节第一拍是清楚的「咚」、后面三拍是轻一点的「嗒」，耳朵一听就知道每组的起点在哪——这是大多数钢琴老师让学生从第一天就跟节拍器练的根本原因。

点下面按钮直接进入主应用，开始时就是 80 BPM 4/4 传统鼓点。每周稳在一个 BPM 不动，下周试着推到 85。坚持一个月，节奏稳定性会有质的变化。
narrative_en:
Starting piano with a metronome? Tempo drift is the #1 stumbling block in the first six months.

80 BPM is the widely-agreed starting tempo — Hanon, Czerny, and Beyer all open their technique sections around this speed. Slower than 80 and the rhythm falls apart from dragging; faster and you start racing the beat before you have earned it. Most beginners who jump to 100 BPM within two weeks end up abandoning the metronome entirely because the gap between their scales and the click grows too obvious.

This page pre-sets 80 BPM, 4/4, traditional drum. The first beat of each bar is a clear accent, the next three lighter — the moment you hear it, you know where each group begins. That is the reason most piano teachers insist on practicing with a metronome from day one.

Hit the button below and you are in the app with 80 BPM 4/4 already set. Stay there for a week before pushing to 85. After a month, your tempo stability takes a real step.

title_zh: 鼓手慢练 60 BPM 节拍器
desc_zh: 鼓手专用的慢练节拍器，60 BPM 4/4 拍，专门用于啃 16 分音符 rudiments（paradiddle、flams、diddles）和军鼓控制力训练。
desc_en: Slow-practice metronome for drummers — 60 BPM, 4/4, traditional drum. Built for working on 16th-note rudiments (paradiddles, flams, diddles) and snare control at practice tempo.
narrative_zh:
鼓手练 paradiddle 的时候最常犯的错，就是在谱面上写 80 BPM 就跟着 80 BPM 走，半年后发现自己 16 分音符总含糊、手腕发紧。

正经的练法是先用 60 BPM 把 16 分音符严格「哒哒哒哒」走四遍——重点不是快，是每颗音的时值完全均匀、两手力度完全一致。这个速度上你才有余裕去听自己的「撞点」（sticking attack point）是否一致。等 60 BPM 稳了，再切到 70，按同一套动作再来四遍。

这个页面已经把 BPM 设在 60、4/4 拍，传统鼓点模式——第一个音打强拍（手或脚），后面三下轻一点。打开主应用后开始，第一周只练 60 BPM，第二周开始每周 +5。一两个月后回头看，你会惊讶自己慢练的总时长。
narrative_en:
Most drummers hit the same wall: they read 80 BPM on the page and play 80 BPM from day one, then wonder why their 16th notes get mushy and their wrists tighten up.

The disciplined path is 60 BPM first — strict four-stroke singles, doubles, paradiddles, flams, diddles — every interval of every stroke perfectly even, both hands at identical dynamic. You do not have that kind of bandwidth above 60. Once you are clean there, 70, then 75. Patience is the whole game.

This page sets 60 BPM, 4/4, traditional drum. The first strike of every bar is the accent (your hand or your hi-hat foot), the next three lighter. Hit the button and start. One week at 60, then add five every week. In two months you will be shocked at how much slow time actually adds up.

title_zh: 跑步配速 180 BPM 节拍器
desc_zh: 跑步配速 180 步/分，佳明、Strava 多项研究公认的最优步频，跟拍能改善跑步经济性、降低受伤风险。
desc_en: Running cadence metronome at 180 BPM — the widely-recommended step rate from Garmin and Strava research. Improves running economy and reduces injury risk.
narrative_zh:
180 步/分是过去二十年跑步研究反复确认的「最佳步频」——不管是精英马拉松选手，还是业余跑者，把步频提到 180 附近，膝关节冲击力下降、跑步经济性提高。

大多数人平时自然跑是 160-170，看起来差不多，但步子过大的代价是脚跟着地——跑步伤膝、胫骨前痛、髋部代偿，很多都从这里来。用节拍器盯 180 一两周，等身体习惯了再撤掉，自然就会维持。

这个页面已经设到 180 BPM、4/4 拍，均匀节拍（每拍等响，强调节奏而不是强弱）。跑步时放在口袋里，每响一下对应一步——不用看屏幕，听节奏对齐脚步就行。刚开始觉得「跑得快了累」，那是步幅还没降下来，三五次之后步频会自动让步幅小一些。
narrative_en:
180 steps per minute is the cadence that twenty years of running research keeps coming back to — elite marathoners and weekend joggers alike. Get your cadence up near 180 and the heel-strike mechanics that wreck knees start to fade. Running economy improves, ground reaction force drops.

Most people self-select at 160-170. Close enough that it feels fine, but the over-striding that comes with it is exactly what loads the joints badly. Train with a metronome at 180 for a couple of weeks, then take it off — your body keeps the new pattern.

This page is set to 180 BPM, 4/4, uniform click (every beat equal weight, no accents, so it is just a step-clock). Pocket the phone, match your footfalls to the click, do not look at the screen. The first few runs feel weirdly fast — that is your stride length dropping, which is the whole point.

title_zh: 6/8 拍节拍器（jig 与爱尔兰民谣）
desc_zh: 6/8 复合拍号节拍器，jig、Irish folk、美国乡村摇滚常用拍号。90 BPM 是大多数 jig 教学曲目的标准起步速度。
desc_en: 6/8 compound-time metronome, the time signature of jigs, Irish folk, and American roots music. 90 BPM is the standard starting tempo for most jig tutorials.
narrative_zh:
6/8 拍是「复合拍号」里最常遇到的那个——学吉他 fiddling、班卓琴、蓝草、爱尔兰民谣、jig、jazz waltz，几乎都要面对它。它听起来是 6 拍，但实际分组是「2+2+2」，每组三拍、共有两组——心里的拍子是 2 而不是 6。

这个页面预设 90 BPM、6/8 拍、传统鼓点。传统鼓点模式里，每个 8 分音符都有清楚的强弱对比（强 - 弱 - 弱 - 强 - 弱 - 弱），三拍一循环、两组一循环——听起来是「哒哒哒 · 哒哒哒」这种火车轮转的节奏感，就是 jig 最标志性的律动。

点开主应用后，先跟着拍子用脚打一组六拍（强 - 弱 - 弱 · 强 - 弱 - 弱），等一周弄清楚了，再上手弹拨。复合拍号最初几周会反复「回到 4/4 思考」，这是正常的——多跟拍就内化了。
narrative_en:
6/8 is the compound time signature everyone meets eventually — fiddle tunes, banjo, bluegrass, Irish folk, jazz waltzes. There are six eighth notes per bar, but they group in 2s, so the pulse you actually feel is 2, not 6. Counting "one-and-a, two-and-a" gets you there.

This page is set to 90 BPM, 6/8, traditional drum. The drum mode gives you a clear accent on the downbeat of each group: BUM-bum-bum · BUM-bum-bum. That rhythmic lilt is the entire feel of a jig — once it is in your body, the tune basically plays itself.

Open the app and tap your foot through six notes (BUM-bum-bum · BUM-bum-bum) for a while before you ever pick up the instrument. Your brain will fight this for the first two weeks — it keeps wanting to count to four. That is normal. Stay with it; the compound meter sinks in around week three.

desc_zh: 3/4 拍节拍器，专为华尔兹、圆舞曲、三步舞设计。100 BPM 是入门学员最舒服的旋转速度。
desc_en: 3/4 time metronome, built for waltzes and Viennese-style dance. 100 BPM is the most comfortable rotation speed for beginners.
narrative_zh:
3/4 拍子是「强 - 弱 - 弱」三拍一组，每一组对应华尔兹里的一步（一、二、三）。它跟 4/4 的区别不是「少一拍」，是「节奏重心变了」——4/4 听感是稳定的、几乎正方形的（强 - 弱 - 次强 - 弱），3/4 是转圈的、不断「回原点」的弧线。

这个页面预设 100 BPM、3/4 拍、传统鼓点——第一拍明显的「咚」、第二第三拍轻一点的「嗒嗒」。如果是初学华尔兹舞步，跟着这个拍子练 box step（一格一格地）：听到「咚」就是迈第一步，听到第二、第三下就是转身、收脚。

100 BPM 是初学者最舒服的速度——高级选手舞伴可能跳到 130-180 的快速维也纳华尔兹，那是熟练后的事。刚开始就是 100，把「咚 - 嗒 - 嗒」的律动印到身体里再提速。
narrative_en:
3/4 time is "strong - weak - weak" — three beats per bar, one step per bar in a waltz. It is not just 4/4 with a beat cut off. The pulse feels circular rather than square: every bar returns to the same starting position, which is why waltzing feels like turning around your partner instead of progressing across a floor.

This page is set to 100 BPM, 3/4, traditional drum — clear downbeat on beat 1, lighter on beats 2 and 3. If you are learning the box step, the downbeat is the first step; beat 2 is the side step; beat 3 is the closing step back to where you started.

100 BPM is the right beginner speed. Viennese waltz goes 130-180+ BPM, but that is a different skill level. Stay at 100 until the "strong-weak-weak" feels automatic, then push.

title_zh: 儿童学琴数拍子节拍器（童音模式）
desc_zh: 为儿童钢琴启蒙设计的节拍器，70 BPM 4/4 拍 + 童音数拍模式，每拍会念出「一二三四」，帮小朋友脱离家长陪数、独自练琴。
desc_en: Metronome for kids starting piano — 70 BPM, 4/4, with a voice-count mode that calls out "one two three four" each bar. Lets children practice solo without a parent counting for them.
narrative_zh:
小孩学琴最让家长头疼的事：练琴时数拍子走神、看着谱速度乱、自己练跟老师带节奏差一截。

童音模式就是为了这一步设计的——节拍器每拍会用童声念出「一、二、三、四」，相当于节拍器自带一个不累、不抱怨、永远耐心的陪练。家长去做饭、刷剧都没关系，孩子打开页面、点开始，就有声音跟着数拍。

70 BPM 是儿童启蒙最稳的速度——太慢孩子会想着玩别的，太快就跟不上。这个区间里孩子的注意力还能稳住，眼、手、耳能同步。点开主应用后默认就是这个配置。第一次只让孩子跟着声音拍手（一组四拍），拍顺了再上手弹。

一周后如果孩子能稳定跟到 60 秒不乱，再调高到 80 试试。
narrative_en:
Parents of young piano students know the drill: the kid loses count, stares at the page, drags through the piece half-tempo, then somehow still can not find beat 1.

Voice mode fixes exactly that step. The metronome calls out "one, two, three, four" in a child-friendly voice on every beat — the kid has a built-in practice buddy that does not get tired, does not check its phone, and never raises its voice. You can go make dinner.

70 BPM is the right starting tempo for this age — slow enough that attention holds, fast enough that it still feels like music. Open the app and let the kid clap along with the voice for a minute before they touch the keyboard. Once they can sustain it for a full minute without breaking, push to 80.

desc_zh: 吉他练习节拍器，100 BPM 4/4 拍对应大多数吉他 TAB 谱的默认速度。均匀节拍模式适合节奏型拨弦练习。
desc_en: Guitar practice metronome at 100 BPM — the default tempo of most guitar TAB charts. Uniform click is ideal for strumming pattern practice.
narrative_zh:
吉他谱子（特别是 TAB）经常印着「♩ = 100」之类——100 BPM 是民谣吉他入门绝大多数练习曲、教学曲的标准速度。

这个页面设到 100 BPM、4/4、均匀节拍（每拍响度一致，没有强弱区分）。均匀节拍的好处是听不清「每小节起点」——但对练吉他节拍型（扫弦、分解）反而是好事：你不会被强拍带跑，注意力全在「我每一拍都准不准」。

练习节奏型时，把节拍器当作每拍的同步点——「下 - 下下 - 上 - 下下」这种 16 分节奏型，每响一拍对应一个动作。第一次练不快不要紧，只要每个动作都对齐响点，三个月下来你会发现自己的节奏感有了根本变化。
narrative_en:
Most guitar TAB charts print a tempo marking around 100 BPM — folk, pop, and acoustic practice pieces all default there. 100 is the right universal speed for adult beginners.

This page is set to 100 BPM, 4/4, uniform click (every beat equal weight, no accents). For strumming patterns specifically, uniform beats are actually better than drum-style accents — you stop relying on the downbeat to find your place and instead focus on whether every single strum lands cleanly on the click.

Count "down-down-up-up-down-up" against each beat. The first three weeks will feel like a lot of work, but your timing will fundamentally change. After a month with a uniform click you cannot go back to playing without one.

desc_zh: 舞蹈课专用节拍器，120 BPM 对应 hip-hop、jazz、k-pop 编舞的中速分段，适合课后单独跑动作。
desc_en: Dance class metronome at 120 BPM — the middle tempo for hip-hop, jazz, and K-pop choreography. Useful for drilling moves solo after class.
narrative_zh:
120 BPM 是当代流行舞蹈（hip-hop、jazz funk、k-pop 编舞）里最常见的「中速」——不快不慢，可以练动作、可以跑节奏，可以检查每个 8 拍的对齐。

舞蹈课后自己回去跑动作，最容易丢的是「8 拍没数准」——一段 8 拍的 phrase 跑到第 7 拍乱了，重来。这个页面把节拍器设到 120，均匀节拍（每个 8 分音符都响一下），你可以把每两个 4 拍想成一组 phrase，强拍由你自己身体去找。

更进阶一点的方法：把每响两个当作一组「嗒 - 哒」（一组 2 拍），每响八个当作一 phrase，跟自己当天学的动作对齐。比自己心里默数稳得多。
narrative_en:
120 BPM is the universal "middle tempo" of contemporary street dance — hip-hop, jazz funk, K-pop choreography all sit there. Not too fast to drill, not too slow to feel like music.

When you practice moves solo after class, the thing that goes wrong first is usually count drift — an 8-count phrase that lands on the wrong beat by the second run-through. Open this page, run the metronome at 120, uniform click, and let each beat be a checkpoint for your body.

A trick that helps: think of every two clicks as a sub-beat pair, every eight clicks as one phrase. Match the movement to the click directly. Eight counts in, you know exactly where you are.

title_zh: 民乐练习节拍器（2/4 拍）
desc_zh: 民乐练习节拍器，2/4 拍（二拍子）古筝、笛子、琵琶、扬琴练习曲的通用拍号。90 BPM 适合传统曲目慢练。
desc_en: Practice metronome for Chinese traditional instruments — 2/4 time (二拍子) is the standard signature for guzheng, dizi, pipa, and yangqin repertoire. 90 BPM works well for slow traditional pieces.
narrative_zh:
民乐练习曲大量使用 2/4 拍——古筝、笛子、琵琶、二胡、扬琴的入门和考级曲，几乎都是 2/4 拍（少数 3/4、4/4，或 6/8）。它跟西方 4/4 不同——没有「强 - 弱 - 次强 - 弱」的方块感，而是「重 - 轻」两拍一组，强弱对比鲜明、节奏紧凑。

这个页面预设 90 BPM、2/4 拍、传统鼓点。第一拍「咚」、第二拍「嗒」——小军鼓鼓点的那种干脆感，正好对应很多民乐曲子里「板眼」节奏型（板 = 重拍，眼 = 弱拍）。

如果练的是流派性强的曲子（比如江南丝竹、广东音乐），除了 2/4 还会有 1/4、3/8、加花等。要严格按板眼跟拍，光听「咚」是不是踩在板上是关键——这就是这个传统鼓点模式比均匀模式好的地方。
narrative_en:
2/4 (二拍子) is the workhorse time signature of Chinese traditional music — guzheng, dizi, pipa, erhu, yangqin repertoire, beginner pieces and graded exam pieces alike. Unlike Western 4/4 it does not feel "square"; it pulses in a hard "strong-weak" two-beat pattern, very tight, very crisp.

This page is set to 90 BPM, 2/4, traditional drum — clear downbeat on beat 1, lighter on beat 2. That pattern matches the "板眼" (ban-yan) rhythmic structure of many traditional pieces, where 板 is the heavy beat and 眼 is the light one.

For more idiomatic regional styles (Jiangnan silk-and-bamboo, Cantonese music), you will also encounter 1/4, 3/8, and ornamental variations. The disciplined approach is to make sure your 板 always lands exactly on the downbeat. That is what traditional drum mode gives you, and what uniform mode would hide.

desc_zh: 40 BPM 极慢练节拍器，慢中求稳专用速度。钢琴和弦连接、歌唱呼吸控制、瑜伽体式停留都常用这个速度。
desc_en: 40 BPM ultra-slow practice metronome — for chord transitions, breath control, and slow-movement drills where tempo stability matters more than speed.
narrative_zh:
40 BPM 听起来像个笑话——每拍 1.5 秒，几乎是「站着不动」的速度。但这个速度恰恰是钢琴和弦连接、歌唱换气、瑜伽体式停留、太极单式练习最常用的「灵魂速度」。

原因不是要学得慢，而是要在慢里找到每个动作之间的「缝隙」——和弦从 C 换到 G 的过程中有几个微动作、用多少手指发力、呼吸换在哪一拍落点。把这些动作每个都拆开来做，每个都在 40 BPM 这一拍里完成得彻底干净，再正常速度练时就不乱了。

这个页面预设 40 BPM、4/4 拍、童音数拍模式——40 BPM 时均匀响点的强拍提示反而显得稀疏，童声每拍念「一、二、三、四」帮你数拍不丢。打开主应用，专注每个动作的当下 1.5 秒内容，两周后切到 60 BPM 看效果，差异会让你吃惊。
narrative_en:
40 BPM sounds like a joke — 1.5 seconds per beat. But this is the speed that serious slow-practice methodology is built on: piano chord transitions, breath control in singing, yoga asana holds, tai chi single-posture drilling.

The point is not to learn slowly. The point is to find the gaps between movements. The micro-actions inside a C-to-G chord change, the precise breath placement before a phrase, the exact muscle sequence in a lunge. At 40 BPM you have time to notice every one of them, fix every one of them, then speed up.

This page is set to 40 BPM, 4/4, voice count. At 40 the uniform click gets sparse, so the child voice calling out the beat keeps your internal count from drifting. Open the app, focus entirely on the 1.5 seconds inside each beat. After two weeks, push to 60 and watch the difference.
